clue.text: Common sorts left to the end

blocks.note: genera are kinds or classes, the plural of genus
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Ordinary types of people get left behind until last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the end' tells you to put the left letter after the sorts.
explanation.definitionFit: Something general is shared widely or prevalent, the same sense as calling a belief common.

clue.text: Exceptionally endearing — so cordial

indicators.note: exceptionally means out of the usual way, so the letters leave their usual order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is unusually charming, and therefore warm and friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cordial' reads as an adjective meaning friendly, but here it is a noun, a sweet syrupy drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenadine is a sweet pomegranate syrup, a type of cordial used to flavour drinks.

clue.text: Offensive in which no-one will take part

blocks.note: no as written, and one as the Roman numeral I
some means a part or portion

explanation.surface: A military attack that nobody wants to join.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offensive' looks like a noun, an attack, but it is the adjective meaning unpleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisome means disgusting or foul-smelling, so something noisome is offensive to the senses.

clue.text: Keeping note “X" turned it on

indicators.note: turned means twisted round into a different shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
X is the Roman numeral for ten
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone holding on to a letter marked with a cross found it arousing.
explanation.definitionFit: Retention is the act of holding on to or retaining something, which is the noun sense of keeping.

clue.text: Become engaged and bolt

blocks.note: first meaning: of gears or parts, to engage and catch fast
second meaning: to fasten a door securely

explanation.surface: A couple get engaged and then run away together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engaged' suggests betrothal and 'bolt' suggests running off; both are really about mechanical fastening.
explanation.definitionFit: Mechanical parts interlock and jam when they engage, and securing a door shut with a fastener is the same verb.

clue.text: A male wearing a cast-off may appear embarrassed

indicators.note: whoever is wearing something is wrapped inside it, so one part goes inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
to shed something is to cast it off; split around the inserted pair
A as written plus M, the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A man dressed in somebody's discarded clothes might well look awkward and self-conscious.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'a' plus the cast-off make A SHED, and the 'A male' pair sits inside the shed.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling ashamed and feeling embarrassed are close synonyms, both describing discomfort over one's conduct or situation.

clue.text: Dexterity may be built into a 8

indicators.note: something built is constructed from parts, so the letters are assembled in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
a as written, and 8 is the answer to clue 8-down, an outfit

explanation.surface: Skill might be sewn into a frock by a dressmaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Into' reads as a link word, but its letters are part of the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroitness is skill and nimbleness in using the hands or mind, the same as dexterity.

clue.text: The man occupied by gold's a beast

indicators.note: a place occupied by someone has them inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: he is the pronoun for a man
or is gold in heraldry, with the s from the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A man obsessed with money is described as an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the heraldic word for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse is a large four-legged animal, and beast is a general word for any such creature.

clue.text: Alcoholic liquor created unique artist

blocks.note: made means created
unique means one of a kind, and one is the Roman numeral I
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A drink invented by a one-of-a-kind painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Madeira is a fortified wine from the Portuguese island of that name, a strong alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Groom's outfit

blocks.note: first meaning: to tidy or prepare
second meaning: a garment or set of clothes

explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks what the bridegroom wears; the two words are separate senses, one a verb and one a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To groom or dress hair or a horse is to tidy it, and a frock is a set of clothes, an outfit.

clue.text: He wrote “Labour, a Way Back"

indicators.note: going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: toil is hard labour
a way or direction: E for east, a compass point

explanation.surface: It reads like the title of a political memoir about returning the Labour Party to power.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks pretend to frame a book title; they actually frame the wordplay. T. S. Eliot and George Eliot are both writers.
explanation.definitionFit: T. S. Eliot was a poet and playwright, author of The Waste Land, so he is a man who wrote.

clue.text: What the marksman needs is transport to the range

blocks.note: a cart is a simple vehicle for transport
a ridge is a range of hills

explanation.surface: A shooter needs a lift out to the firing range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Range' points at a shooting range, but here it means a line of hills.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartridge holds the bullet and powder that a rifleman loads before firing.

clue.text: Sum for which doctor's been let in by relation

indicators.note: being let in by someone means being admitted inside them, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: an aunt is a relation; split after its first letter
MO is Medical Officer, a doctor; the 's is 'has'

explanation.surface: A family member lets the doctor into the house to settle the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: An amount is a total or quantity, the same thing as a sum of money or figures.

clue.text: The latter years of Einstein perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the word is only one possible version of its letters, so they can be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: It reads like a biography chapter about the scientist's final decades.
explanation.definitionFit: The last ten years of a century, numbered ninety to ninety-nine, come latest in it.

clue.text: In conversation, misinform adolescent

indicators.note: in conversation means as spoken, so the word is judged by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: said slowly, the verb sounds like a young lady in a class at school

explanation.surface: Someone tells lies to a teenager while chatting.
explanation.walkthrough: A form is a school class and Miss is a girl's title, so a Miss in a form is a pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl attending school is typically a child or teenager, so she is a young adolescent.

clue.text: A little plaice, nicely cooked, is enough for old people

indicators.note: a little of the following words means only a short stretch of their letters is taken

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the fish and the start of the adverb
surface padding only: it adds to the kitchen picture and gives no letters

explanation.surface: A small portion of well-cooked flatfish is plenty for elderly diners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooked' tempts you towards an anagram, but it is only decoration. Plaice is a flatfish eaten in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iceni were an ancient British tribe, Boudicca's people, so they are a people from long ago.

clue.text: Learn to exert force

blocks.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn
to strain is to exert oneself

explanation.surface: An instruction to master the skill of applying pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exert force' looks like one phrase; split it so 'force' stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To constrain someone is to compel or restrict them, which is what forcing them does.

clue.text: Will meant to reorganise following an investigation

indicators.note: reorganising means putting things into a new arrangement, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: a test is an investigation or trial
taken as written

explanation.surface: A legacy document was intended to be rewritten after an inquiry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' means the rearranged letters come after the investigation.
explanation.definitionFit: A last will and testament is the legal document setting out what happens to a person's estate.

clue.text: The state of modern knitwear

blocks.note: new means modern
a jersey is a knitted pullover

explanation.surface: A remark about the condition of today's sweaters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' seems to mean condition; it is an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: New Jersey is one of the fifty states of the USA, on the east coast.

clue.text: Faulty one — or sure to become faulty

indicators.note: letters that become faulty are broken up and put together wrongly in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A defective item, or one certain to go wrong soon.
explanation.definitionFit: Erroneous means mistaken or containing errors, and faulty describes something with defects or mistakes.

clue.text: Taking a chance, hide cutting gear

indicators.note: a thing cutting into another enters it, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: a rig is equipment or gear
a hide is an animal's skin

explanation.surface: A gamble: concealing gear for cutting things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' reads as a verb meaning conceal, but it is the noun for an animal's pelt.
explanation.definitionFit: Risking something means exposing it to danger on a gamble, which is taking a chance.

clue.text: A means of fixing pay

blocks.note: first meaning: a threaded metal fastener
second meaning: old British slang for wages or salary

explanation.surface: A way of rigging someone's wages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fixing pay' suggests setting or rigging wages; the two senses split at 'fixing'.
explanation.definitionFit: A threaded fastener holds things together, and in British slang the word also means a person's weekly wage.

clue.text: Putting RAF officers into existing accommodation

indicators.note: into means going inside, so one piece is placed within the other
accommodation is a place that houses something, so it holds the other piece

blocks.note: real means actually existing
POs are Pilot Officers, a junior RAF rank

explanation.surface: Billeting air force officers in the quarters that already exist.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAF is the Royal Air Force, Britain's air arm.
explanation.definitionFit: Reposal is an old noun for the act of reposing or placing something, as in putting trust in someone.

clue.text: Sweet dough with harmful content

indicators.note: a content is what is held inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: paste is a dough of flour and fat
ill can mean harmful, as in ill effects

explanation.surface: A sweet pastry with a poisonous filling, as in a fairy tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastille is a small chewable sweet or lozenge, so it is a confection.

clue.text: Quiet and fearful when handled clumsily

blocks.note: p is piano, the musical direction for quiet
awed means filled with fear or wonder

explanation.surface: Someone goes silent and scared when groped.
explanation.definitionFit: Pawed means touched or fumbled at awkwardly, as an animal's feet might do.

clue.text: A little place that's not lived in by the owner

blocks.note: the 's is short for is

blocks.clueFragment: not lived in by the owner
blocks.note: a property let is rented out to tenants

explanation.surface: A small property kept by a landlord who lives elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place' suggests a house or flat; read it as a tiny bit of land in water.
explanation.definitionFit: An islet is a very small island, so it is a little spot of land.

clue.text: There's some depression about the pages being spotty (6. The solution of Saturday's Prize Puzzle No 18,262 will appear next Saturday

indicators.note: about means around, so one word is placed round the other

blocks.note: a dale is a valley, a depression in the land
pp is the abbreviation for pages

blocks.clueFragment: The solution of Saturday's Prize Puzzle No 18,262 will appear next Saturday
blocks.note: not part of the clue: a newspaper notice that the scan ran into the clue text

explanation.surface: A dip in the ground surrounding speckled sheets of paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue runs into a newspaper notice after the word count; only the words up to spotty belong to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dapple describes a coat or surface marked with round patches or spots, like a dapple-grey horse.

clue.text: Correct for the current rise

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means going upwards, so the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a tide is a current of the sea

explanation.surface: It sounds like a demand to fix the present price increase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like an adjective meaning present, but it is a flow of water.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit a text is to revise it and put its mistakes right, which is to correct it.

clue.text: Blast the twister!

blocks.note: surface reading: a curse on some cheating trickster
setter's reading: a blast of air that spins, a tornado

explanation.walkthrough: 'Blast' is an oath and 'twister' a swindler, but both words also describe a violent rotating gust.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirlwind is a column of air spinning rapidly, a gusty storm often called a twister.

clue.text: Moderates like filling in survey return

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the word is read backwards
a filling goes inside something, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: to survey is to look at, see
as means like, in the same way as

explanation.surface: Someone tempers their opinions, like padding a questionnaire's answers.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease something is to lessen or soften it, just as moderating tones it down.

clue.text: Using only the fingers? No hands

blocks.note: first meaning: done with the digits, the fingers
second meaning: a watch showing numbers rather than having hands

explanation.walkthrough: Fingers are digits, so the word whimsically means by finger; a clock or watch with a number display has no hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Digit is the anatomical word for a finger, and a digital timepiece displays numerals instead of moving pointers.

clue.text: Having to agree without reservation

blocks.note: taken as written
figures that tally agree with each other

explanation.surface: Being obliged to consent with no reservations at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Totally means completely or wholly, the same as doing something without holding anything back.
